mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% over the prior 3 months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during similar high-inflation periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS exceeds 2% month-over-month for two consecutive months, signaling labor market resilience that supports S&P 500 gains in the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns under this labor signal are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) accompanied by a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a shift from supply-side to demand-side constraints, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 10% while INDPRO decreases by > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when the signal is active.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below 95 for three consecutive months suggests supply-side softness, which typically precedes S&P 500 drawdowns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during INDPRO < 95 periods are not significantly lower than during expansion phases (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month CPIAUCSL inflation rate crosses above 2% for the first time in a tightening cycle, the S&P 500 is expected to underperform over the next 20 days as investors anticipate future rate hikes.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during such inflation spikes are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) below 250k for two consecutive months indicates weakening labor demand, which tends to depress S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during softening are not statistically lower than during healthy labor markets (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both consumer (HOUST) and business demand (RSAFS) above 800 and 450 million units respectively for a month signals a dual-demand surge that drives S&P 500 gains over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 800 and RSAFS > 450 for the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns under this combined signal are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to supply-side constraints when the industrial production index (INDPRO) lags the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 5 points for three consecutive months predicts S&P 500 declines over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO - CPIAUCSL > 5 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during such imbalance periods are not significantly lower than during balanced regimes (p > 0.05).
